children: The proposed pembrolizumab biosimilar could receive a USFDA decision by Q3 2027, potentially expanding access to cancer treatment in North America

Zydus Lifesciences and Germany-based Formycon AG have received US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) acceptance for review of the Biologics License Application (BLA) for FYB206, a proposed biosimilar to Keytruda (pembrolizumab). According to the companies, this is the first publicly announced acceptance by the US regulator of an application for a proposed Keytruda biosimilar.

Submitted in the third quarter of 2026, the application is expected to undergo a review process that could conclude with a regulatory decision in the third quarter of 2027. The regulatory dossier has also been submitted to Health Canada.

FYB206 was developed without a comparative Phase III efficacy trial, following an approach agreed upon with the USFDA in February 2025. According to Formycon, this pathway helped accelerate development and reduce investment while maintaining the scientific requirements for biosimilar development.

Pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor that blocks the PD-1 receptor and is used to treat several types of cancer. Keytruda remains the world's best-selling biologic medicine, with worldwide sales, including those of its subcutaneous formulation Keytruda Qlex, reaching USD31.7 billion in 2025.

Dr Sharvil P Patel, Managing Director of Zydus Lifesciences, said the application’s acceptance marks an important step towards expanding access to affordable pembrolizumab therapy in the US and Canada. He added that FYB206 could strengthen the company's oncology biosimilars portfolio and support patient access to cancer treatment.

Dr Stefan Glombitza, CEO of Formycon AG, said the regulatory milestone reflects progress in advancing the proposed biosimilar. He highlighted the development pathway agreed upon with the USFDA and the partnership with Zydus to support commercialisation in North America.

Under an exclusive licensing and supply agreement signed in December 2025, Formycon is responsible for development, regulatory submissions and product supply, while Zydus holds commercialisation rights in the US and Canada. Commercialisation remains subject to regulatory approval and resolution of any intellectual property issues. The acceptance of the BLA also triggers a milestone payment to Formycon under the agreement.
The companies aim to expand access to pembrolizumab through FYB206, subject to regulatory clearance and applicable requirements.
